title: Agent Behavioral Contracts: Formal Specification and Runtime Enforcement for Reliable Autonomous AI Agents
tldr: Introduces Agent Behavioral Contracts (ABC), a formal Design-by-Contract framework for autonomous AI agents that defines preconditions, invariants, governance policies, and recovery mechanisms with probabilistic (p,δ,k)-satisfaction guarantees and a proven drift bounds theorem.
problem_and_motivation: AI agents operate on prompts with no formal behavioral specification, causing drift, governance failures, and project failures that traditional software contracts solve. Runtime enforcement is a theoretical necessity: the self-evolution trilemma proves passive safety is provably insufficient for agents that evolve behavior over extended interactions.
approach: Defines ABC contract tuple C = (P, Ihard, Isoft, Ghard, Gsoft, R) with hard/soft constraint separation and recovery mechanisms
Introduces (p, δ, k)-satisfaction: probabilistic compliance where contracts hold with probability p, deviations within δ, and recovery within k steps
Models behavioral drift as an Ornstein–Uhlenbeck process with Lyapunov stability analysis, proving drift converges to D* = α/γ in expectation
Establishes Compositionality Theorem with four sufficient conditions (interface, assumption, governance, recovery) for safe multi-agent chains
Derives probabilistic composition bounds showing reliability degrades multiplicatively and drift accumulates additively across N-agent chains
Implements ContractSpec, a YAML-based DSL for declarative contract specification supporting hard/soft constraints and file-reference composition
Builds AgentAssert runtime enforcement library with sub-10ms per-action overhead and recovery re-prompting for soft violations
Creates AgentContract-Bench benchmark of 200 scenarios across 7 domains with 6 adversarial stress profiles and composition testing
Evaluates across 1,980 sessions on 7 models from 6 vendors measuring soft violations, drift trajectories, and reliability under stress
Applies SPRT-based certification to reduce required sample size from ~18,445 to 150–300 sessions for contract compliance verification
findings: num: Contracted agents detect 5.2–6.8 soft violations per session that uncontracted baselines miss entirely (p < 0.0001, Cohen's d = 6.7–33.8)
num: Hard constraint compliance reaches 88–100% across all models under contract enforcement
num: Behavioral drift bounded to D* < 0.27 across extended 12-turn sessions with OU mean-reversion fit (R² = 0.49–0.75)
num: 100% recovery success for frontier models (GPT-5.2, Claude Opus 4.6), 17–100% across all models
num: Runtime overhead < 10ms per action, scaling linearly at 0.218k + 2.8ms (R² = 0.99) for k constraints
num: Ablation study shows ~0.20 reliability index drop when recovery or soft constraints are removed, consistent across 4 models (σ < 0.01)
num: Platform guardrails (Azure DefaultV2) block 40–60% of legitimate multi-turn sessions when layered with behavioral contracts
num: Stress resilience: hard compliance never drops below 0.911 under adversarial prompt injection across 4 models and 3 attack types
The transparency effect: lower soft compliance scores under contracts indicate measurement, not regression — contracts make invisible violations visible
Recovery transforms exponential compliance decay (q^T) into linear decay (1 − T(1−q)(1−r)), a qualitative shift from unreliable to deployable

key_equations.equation: C = (P, Ihard, Isoft, Ghard, Gsoft, R)
key_equations.explanation: ABC contract tuple: Preconditions, hard and soft Invariants, hard and soft Governance policies, and Recovery mechanisms

key_equations.equation: dD(t) = (α − γ D(t)) dt + σ dW(t)
key_equations.explanation: Ornstein-Uhlenbeck drift dynamics: natural drift α pushes away from specification, contract recovery γ restores, noise σ captures LLM non-determinism
Stationary mean drift: expected drift under contract enforcement equals natural drift rate divided by recovery rate

key_equations.equation: P[D(t) > α/γ + η] ≤ exp(−γ η² / σ²)
key_equations.explanation: Gaussian concentration bound on stationary drift: probability of exceeding mean-plus-η decays exponentially in γ and quadratically in η
Probabilistic composition: end-to-end reliability of two-agent chain is at least the product of individual agent and handoff probabilities

key_equations.equation: pchain ≥ ∏ᵢ pᵢ · ∏ⱼ phⱼ, δchain ≤ ∑ᵢ δᵢ + ∑ⱼ δhⱼ
key_equations.explanation: N-agent composition: reliability degrades multiplicatively, drift accumulates additively (the 'broken telephone' effect)

definitions.definition: Tuple C = (P, Ihard, Isoft, Ghard, Gsoft, R) specifying preconditions, hard and soft invariants, hard and soft governance constraints, and recovery mechanisms for an autonomous AI agent
Probabilistic contract compliance: hard constraints hold with probability ≥ p, soft compliance stays within δ tolerance k steps after any violation
Composite metric wc·D_compliance(t) + wd·D_distributional(t) combining a lagging compliance-gap indicator with a leading JSD-based distributional shift indicator
Empirical finding that contracted agents show lower apparent soft compliance because contracts make previously invisible violations measurable
Weighted composite α1·C̄ + α2·(1−D̄) + α3·1/(1+Ē) + α4·S summarizing an agent's overall contractual fitness across compliance, drift, recovery, and stress resilience
Proof that ABC contracts with recovery rate γ > α bound expected stationary drift to D* = α/γ with Gaussian concentration and a closed-form design criterion
Under interface compatibility, assumption discharge, governance consistency, and recovery independence, individual contract guarantees compose into end-to-end multi-agent guarantees
Lemma showing recovery transforms exponential compliance decay (q^T) into linear decay (1 − T(1−q)(1−r))

topics.name: Concept Drift as the Framework for Progressive Profile Updates
topics.justification: Paper models behavioral drift via Ornstein-Uhlenbeck process with composite drift score D(t) combining compliance gap and JSD distributional shift. The drift detection methodology is transferable to progressive user profile updates in personal finance systems, though the paper's focus is AI agent behavioral drift, not financial user profile drift.

topics.name: ML Model Serving and Deployment
topics.justification: Paper provides runtime enforcement framework for deployed AI agents with formal guarantees. AgentAssert runtime achieves sub-10ms overhead with O(k + |A|) complexity. Establishes principles for monitoring and enforcing constraints on deployed ML systems that inform deployment reliability practices.

topics.name: On-Device vs. Server Inference
topics.justification: Paper measures and optimizes runtime enforcement overhead (<10ms per action at <1% of LLM inference latency). The complexity analysis and linear scaling results inform tradeoffs for where enforcement logic should execute in a deployment architecture.

topic_relevance.contribution_to_field: This paper contributes a formal framework for behavioral governance of autonomous AI agents, but its primary relevance to the Odin personal finance system is methodological. The drift bounds theorem (Ornstein-Uhlenbeck modeling with Lyapunov stability analysis) provides a mathematical foundation for detecting and bounding behavioral drift that could transfer to financial user profile drift monitoring. The hard/soft constraint separation in the ABC contract tuple mirrors Odin's constraint encoding for budget recommendations (protected, locked, open categories). The runtime enforcement architecture demonstrates how to achieve sub-10ms overhead for constraint checking in production systems. The paper's empirical methodology — controlled experiments with statistical rigor across multiple models — provides a template for evaluating ML system reliability.
directly_justifies: Profile drift monitoring using composite detection metrics combining compliance and distributional signals
limits: Focuses on AI agent behavioral drift, not financial user profile drift — no direct transfer of experimental results
State dictionary assumption requires pre-computed features from raw data, a separate challenge in personal finance context
Reference distribution calibration requires dedicated calibration runs with no automated staleness detection
Financial domain evaluation limited to 10 tasks over 6-turn sessions — broader validation needed for personal finance applicability
Results are contract-relative: compliance metrics depend on constraint specificity, not absolute agent quality
topic_relevance.topic_mapping_rationale: Systematically scanned the 14-topic Odin taxonomy for cross-cutting themes. 5.B.I (concept drift for adaptive user modeling) was selected for the drift detection methodology using JSD divergence and Ornstein-Uhlenbeck modeling, which is the most direct methodological transfer. 14.B (ML serving/deployment) was selected for the runtime enforcement architecture and overhead analysis. 14.C (on-device vs. server inference) was selected for the complexity-driven deployment tradeoff analysis. Topics 3.C.I (hard/soft constraint encoding) was considered but excluded because the paper's constraint types (invariants, governance) address AI agent behavior rather than financial allocations, though the hard/soft distinction is conceptually parallel.

limitations: State dictionary assumption: ABC evaluator requires pre-computed structured features (tone_score, pii_detected) — feature extraction from raw outputs is outside framework scope
Reference distribution calibration requires dedicated calibration runs; no automated staleness detection for non-stationary deployment environments
Recovery is monitoring by default: AgentAssert emits events but deployers must implement domain-specific recovery logic for each constraint
k-window stationarity assumption: drift bounds theorem assumes proximity to stationary distribution; transient phase may be non-negligible for short sessions
Compositionality under correlated failures: probability bounds become optimistic when agents share the same underlying LLM due to correlated failure modes
Benchmark circularity: AgentContract-Bench tests engine consistency against synthetic traces, not behavioral detection in live agent behavior
remember_this: ABC brings Design-by-Contract to AI agents with (p, δ, k)-satisfaction
Transparency effect: contracts reveal violations, not create them
Drift bound D* = α/γ with Gaussian concentration proven via OU model
Recovery transforms exponential decay to linear decay (Lemma 3.10)
